conviction_note: The quarter has been public since 2026-11-03, so the print turns on two things: the Q4 guide, which the CFO has signalled will be cautious ('typical prudence'), and the first management comment since OPay's IPO was pulled, which took the stock down about 20% between 10-28 and 11-02. The cautious guide (small negatives: guide prudence, Google Search slowing, the last beat-and-raise being sold) roughly offsets the low bar left by the OPay drawdown and the buyback capacity (small positives). p_up is 47 on an abs_move of 6.5, giving -0.39. The findings sum to -0.70: the same lean, measured separately.

expectations.real_bar: A Q4 revenue guide whose midpoint is at or above about $203m (FY at least $740m, the top half of the current range), with no new OPay-linked or China-regulatory negative on the call. A guide midpoint at the old implied $201m or lower, combined with the slowdown already visible in Q3, is the setup that sold the August beat.

next_guide.basis: The CFO said on 11-03 that the later reporting date lets management 'approach our final Q4 guidance with our typical prudence'. On the Q2 call management said it had built in a 'more normalized Q4 spike'. Q3 growth slowed (query 21%->17%, ads 27%->22%), and Google Search grew 12% in Q3 against 17% in Q2. Read together, this points to a Q4 guide around the implied $201m midpoint, i.e. FY maintained or narrowed near $736-740m: at or slightly below the street, not a raise.

findings.finding: On 2026-11-03 the CFO said Opera will set its 'final Q4 guidance with our typical prudence'. The FY guide of $734-742m implies Q4 revenue of $197.4-205.4m (+11-16% y/y, midpoint $201.4m) after a +20% Q3. The street's derived Q4 of about $203.4m (FY $740.0m) sits in the upper half of that range, so a 'prudent' Q4 guide is more likely to land at or below the street than above it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance has moved this stock both ways. The initial FY26 guide plus a $300m buyback (2026-02-26) bought +23.38%. The FY raise with Q2 (2026-08-19) was sold -7.12%.
findings.why_not_priced: The prudence remark has been public for two weeks, and the stock is roughly flat since 11-03 ($15.47 to $15.36), so some caution is in. But the street FY figure still sits at $740m, in the upper half of the range. If the market had priced a guide below the street, FY estimates would have come down toward the $738m midpoint. The StockAnalysis FY range ($735.8-744.4m) shows no such cut.
findings.independence: Shares the 11-03 document with the Q3-deceleration finding. Independent support: the Q2 call transcript, where management said it built in a 'more normalized Q4 spike' (https://www.webull.com/news/15429727749776384), and Google's Q3 search slowdown (separate finding).

findings.finding: Alphabet's Q3 2026 Google Search & other revenue grew 12% y/y ($63.35bn), slowing from 17% in Q2, and was flat quarter on quarter (+$79m). That points to a slower search monetisation trend going into Opera's Q4 query line.
findings.link: Google is Opera's main search partner. Query revenue was $62.1m of $178.1m in Q2 2026 (35% of revenue). An analyst put Google at about a third of Opera's revenue at the Sept 2025 Citi conference; the CFO did not confirm it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Opera's query growth went 16% (Q4'25) -> 21% (Q2'26) -> 17% (Q3'26). The Q3 slowdown was in the 11-03 pre-release, and the stock rose 4.46% that day.
findings.why_not_priced: Alphabet's print is public, but the transmission to Opera's Q4 query guide has not been stated by Opera. A priced read would have shown up as cuts to OPRA's FY estimates after 10-28, and none are visible.
findings.independence: Alphabet 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001652044/000165204426000080/googexhibit991q32026.htm). Opera's own Q3 query slowdown (pre-release) points the same way. This is a proxy: Opera's query revenue is driven by value per search, not Google's total.

findings.finding: The pre-released Q3 slowed on both lines: query +17% (Q2 +21%), advertising +22% (Q2 +27%), total +20% (Q2 +25%). Revenue of $182.8m landed 'at the top end' of the $181-183m guide, where Q2 had landed 'beyond the high end' (beat cushion about $0 against $2-3m before).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock rose 4.46% on the 11-03 pre-release, so the market read these numbers as fine on the day.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: it is the pre-released quarter. It is filed because the full release adds segment detail and margins that may sharpen the slowdown story. It is sized near zero under the pre-release rule.
findings.independence: Same 11-03 document as the guide-prudence finding. The Q2 figures come from the Q2 6-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001737450/000173745026000014/opra-ex99_1.htm).

findings.finding: OPRA fell 20.5% ($18.64 on 10-28 to $14.81 on 11-02) when OPay halted its $304m NYSE IPO on 2026-10-30 after a last-minute foreign (reportedly Chinese) regulatory inquiry. OPay had priced 16m ADSs at $19 (about $4bn valuation). Opera's 9.5% stake was carried at about $294.6m at YE2025 ($3.1bn valuation), roughly 22% of Opera's ~$1.36bn market cap. The 11-17 call is management's first chance to comment on the stake and the inquiry.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no prior earnings reaction on OPay. The 10-29/10-30 tape (-6.8%, -11.3% on about 2x volume) shows the stock trades the stake hard.
findings.why_not_priced: The drawdown (about $300m of market cap) is about equal to the whole OPay stake at its YE2025 carrying value, while the IPO was priced at a higher valuation than that carrying value and Bloomberg reports it is paused, not dead (weetracker 11-05). If the market saw the stake as merely delayed, the stock would sit nearer $17-18. The risk to this sign: the reported China inquiry runs through Zhou Yahui, also Opera's controlling shareholder via Kunlun, so part of the discount may be a China-link discount on Opera itself, which the call cannot remove. That caveat is why the finding is sized below 1.
findings.independence: Weetracker 2026-11-05 on revival talks (https://weetracker.com/?p=91353). Carrying value from launchbaseafrica 2026-04-24 (https://launchbaseafrica.com/2026/04/24/an-85-chance-of-a-3-1bn-ipo-within-two-years-inside-operas-high-stakes-opay-bet/). Prices from the Yahoo chart.

findings.why_not_priced: Targets are stale relative to the OPay drop. A price this far below every target says the sell side has not cut, so a 'reassuring' call has room. This is weak evidence: unanimous-Buy names often stay cheap.

findings.finding: This name has sold its last operating beat-and-raise. Q2 beat the top of guide and raised the FY guide, and the stock fell 7.12%. Only the initial FY guide plus a $300m buyback (+23.38%) and the Q4'25 and Q3'26 pre-releases (+13.53%, +4.46%) were bought.

findings.finding: About $272m remains on the $300m two-year buyback ($28.1m used through 2026-06-30, against $145.2m of cash and $64.3m of H1 operating cash flow). The stock now trades 11% below the Q2 average repurchase price of $17.44, so the release or call could carry a stepped-up buyback.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The $300m authorisation announced with Q4'25 on 2026-02-26 was part of a +23.38% day.
findings.why_not_priced: Inference only. No statement of intent has been found. The pace so far has been slow ($11.1m in Q2), and Kunlun sells pro rata into it, which limits the float effect.
findings.independence: Kunlun's pro-rata sale agreement with the issuer (Form 4 / 13D/A, https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/OPRA/schedule-13d-a-opera-ltd-amended-major-shareholder-report-cb457cad2dc0.html).

findings.finding: Mid-quarter statements: on 2026-11-03 and 2026-11-05 Opera announced desktop MAUs of 100m in October (record, +16% y/y, against 94m in Q2). The CFO said results were pre-released because of a 'later-than-usual reporting date'; Q3'25 was reported around 2025-10-28.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: +4.46% on 11-03. The stock fell 5.5% on 11-05, the day of the 100m PC-user release, when OPay/China headlines were also running.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely public. The release will add total MAU, ARPU and MiniPay wallets (18m in June), which feed the FY27 story but not the Q4 number. The reason for the late date is unexplained, which is odd: it fell during OPay's IPO window, but no source links the two.

findings.finding: At the Citi TMT conference in 2025 the CFO said future Google search agreements default to one-year terms, where they had typically run three years. On an annual-renewal contract worth about a third of revenue, any renewal comment on the call is a guide risk in either direction.
findings.why_not_priced: Over a year old and no renewal event is dated. Filed at zero as context for the query line.

baseline_tension: The baseline (20d -12.9%, upside-paid skew) leans slightly positive. My guide findings lean negative and the OPay overhang leans positive, so on balance the evidence agrees with neither strongly and p_up sits near 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 7 (sign against skew): the guide-prudence negative cut from -1.5 to -1.2, because it runs against an upside-paid skew. Not cut further: the chain's 104% ATM spread makes the skew weak.

Rule 6 (bar from one source): the street Q4 figure is derived from a single FY consensus source, which reinforces the small cap on the guide finding (no further cut, to avoid applying the same concern twice).
Rule 5 (proxy): the Google Search counterparty finding cut from -0.5 to -0.4; independence states it is a proxy.
FPI reaction-history lesson: rebuilt the base rate from confirmed releases (median |move| about 7%), which moved abs_move_pct from 6.0 to 6.5. Understatement is the systematic error.
Rule 1 (this name sold its last beat-and-raise): already a filed finding at -0.5; p_up kept near 50 (47), not moved twice.
